title: invocation-burst-lens-and-phase-aware-alert-throttler
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: production token/latency tails are often driven by short invocation bursts (fanout or client retry storms) that do not warrant full SRE paging but do distort SLA and cost dashboards. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: 1) Invocation Burst Lens - new metrics + dashboard panels to surface short-lived burst events and their token/latency composition; 2) Phase-Aware Alert Throttler - an alert smoothing layer that debounces alerts based on invocation phase signatures and burst fingerprints. Summary of changes: added lightweight burst detection at the edge (invocation proxy) that emits invocation.burst_start and invocation.burst_member_count, added histogram and slabbed buckets for burst_duration_seconds and burst_token_count, instrumented runtime to tag spans with invocation_phase (init/prefix/stream/complete) and exposed phase-aware latency quantiles (token_phase_latency_p50/p95/p99), added a Grafana dashboard JSON with burst lens panels and an interactive scatter of burst_token_count vs median token_phase_latency, added an alerting rule that delegates to the new throttler which consults recent burst fingerprints and phase distribution before escalating, added unit and integration tests plus a small e2e perf-canary test to exercise controlled burst generation. Checklist: - [x] Add edge emission of burst markers and phase tags - [x] Runtime: phase annotation on spans and metrics emission - [x] Metrics: histograms, gauges, and exemplar wiring - [x] Dashboard: Grafana JSON + README panel descriptions - [x] Alerting: phase-aware throttler service + alert rule examples - [x] Tests: unit, integration, perf-canary - [x] Docs: observability/notes and migration guide Usage notes: burst markers are low-cardinality and sampled; default sampling = 1/1000 invocations, can be increased per-tenant in the console. The throttler runs as a separate small service in the observability stack and uses a fixed-size in-memory LRU of recent burst fingerprints (configurable TTL) to avoid routing transient spikes to on-call. This is a conservative default — teams can opt-out by turning off the throttler in cluster/overrides. Backwards compatibility: all new metrics follow existing naming conventions and are emitted under the telemetry namespace; consumers that don't understand invocation_phase will fall back to aggregate latency metrics. Impact on cost: modest metric cardinality increase under heavy bursty workloads; recommended retention for burst_* metrics is 14 days by default. Rollout plan: staged on canary region -> staging -> global; feature gated behind OBS_BURST_LENS flag and throttler behind OBS_THROTTLER flag. Related: ENG-1987 (burst detection design), ENG-2043 (alerting ergonomics).

review_comments: Liam Scott (reviewer): Can we keep burst_id cardinality low? Suggest limiting exemplars to 1/10k for high-volume tenants.
Asha Menon (author): Agreed — default sampling is 1/1000 and exemplars are gated by tenant volume; added config knobs and docs note.
Marina Petrova (reviewer): The throttler introduces additional decision hops in alert path — how do we avoid increased alert latency?

Asha Menon (author): Throttler is intended as a pre-filter for paging decisions and runs synchronously with a 50ms budget; we added a circuit-breaker to fall back to ESCALATE when throttler is unhealthy.
Noah Chen (reviewer): Add a test that produces overlapping bursts and verifies dedup behavior.
Asha Menon (author): Added perf-canary scenario 'overlap-burst.yml' and unit tests for fingerprint LRU behavior.
release_notes: Introduces Invocation Burst Lens metrics and a phase-aware alert throttler. New metrics: invocation.burst_count, invocation.burst_member_count, burst_duration_seconds, burst_token_count, token_phase_latency_{p50,p95,p99}. Adds Grafana dashboard 'Invocation Burst Lens' and an optional throttler service to reduce noisy pages during short-lived spikes. Backward-compatible metric names; feature behind OBS_BURST_LENS and OBS_THROTTLER flags.
rollout_plan: canary -> staging -> prod over 3 weeks; default flags off in prod until metrics retention and throttler health checks are validated.
notes_for_oncall: If paging is unexpectedly suppressed after rollout, check throttler logs (/var/log/observability/throttler.log) and circuit-breaker metric observability.throttler.healthy. To force immediate escalation, set OBS_THROTTLER=false in the cluster override and re-evaluate alert rule.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover burst detection heuristics and fingerprint LRU eviction; integration tests validate exemplar propagation and histogram buckets; perf-canary runs simulated micro-bursts and asserts that throttler holds on-call for <80% of synthetic bursts while escalating persistent high p99s.
